requirements.requirement: Containerized web app runs as the unprivileged account appsvc on node1
requirements.summary: appsvc (uid 1001, no shell login mechanism used) was created, subuid/subgid configured, and the nginx container was launched via 'su appsvc' with rootless podman. Post-run process listing shows nginx master process owned by appsvc and workers under the mapped uid 100100, and podman ps confirms the container is owned by the appsvc rootless namespace.

Container published as -p 8080:80; curl to $NODE_IP:8080 and 127.0.0.1:8080 returned HTTP 200 with real HTML content both immediately after launch and after the verified boot cycle. The after-executor global listening-sockets snapshot independently confirms 0.0.0.0:8080 LISTEN owned by the rootless pasta network helper.

A healthy pre-restart baseline was captured (boot_id e561ef47, container Up, HTTP 200). A first real reboot was performed (boot_id changed to 947efb1d) and directly showed boot-time start failing because /run/user/1001 was not created on this init system, with podman stopped and curl returning http:000 — a genuine, evidence-supported failure discovery. The executor fixed this with a custom appsvc-runtimedir OpenRC unit ordered before podman, then performed a second real reboot (boot_id changed again to 935e96cf). Post-second-reboot evidence shows both services 'started' in rc-status, the same container automatically Up 7s with no manual intervention, and curl returning 200 — directly demonstrating the healthy-baseline to disruption to fix to restored-boot-behavior transition required for this class of claim.

requirements.requirement: No active login session for appsvc while the service runs
requirements.summary: who/last/loginctl checks show no TTY or login entries for appsvc both right after manual launch and after the boot-verified restart, while nginx and podman processes run under appsvc's uid. The process tree shows the podman service is launched by root's supervise-daemon invoking podman directly (not by a login shell or su -l), consistent with no session being created.

overall_summary: All four material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: nginx runs under the unprivileged appsvc rootless podman account, is reachable on port 8080, was proven to auto-start at boot through a genuine reboot-discover-fix-reboot-verify cycle, and shows no active login session for appsvc throughout. The executor's node-restart evidence protocol for node1 is well-formed (pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement via connection loss, changed boot identity, and recovered service/app state), matching the independent before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity cross-check. Hygiene is good overall with only minor uncleaned temp-file residue.
limitations: The origin of /tmp/storage-run-1001/{containers,libpod} in the after-executor snapshot is not explained by any single executor command, so it cannot be definitively attributed to a specific action, only inferred as a byproduct of the /run/user/1001 troubleshooting.

No systemd/journal-based service-failure inspection was available (systemctl unsupported on this Alpine/OpenRC image), so failed-service state relies on rc-status output rather than a systemd failed-units enumeration.
Data persistence beyond the container's default image content was not part of this task's contract, so no volume/data-durability check across reboot was necessary or performed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to the task: package installs, user/subuid setup, cgroups enablement, container run/rm iterations, the podman-openrc boot configuration, and the appsvc-runtimedir fix were all directly used to satisfy or verify a material outcome, or were corrective troubleshooting after the first reboot revealed a real boot-start bug (cmd-ade979d4047c44f4, cmd-49dda62eda064460, cmd-bdcb61db5b3c401b, cmd-3301a109782d4206, cmd-2badd10657954ecd, cmd-be1724e8804b476d, cmd-7faf2423fc1e428c — all corrective steps toward the working appsvc-runtimedir/podman boot fix, not unrelated experiments). Two minor items were left as residue and not cleaned up: /tmp/reboot.log and /tmp/reboot2.log (harmless artifacts of the backgrounded reboot commands used for restart verification), and an unexplained /tmp/storage-run-1001/{containers,libpod} directory tree that appears in the after-executor temp-files snapshot but has no corresponding executor command explaining its creation or removal — likely a rootless-podman fallback storage path created during one of the failed /run/user/1001 attempts. None of this weakens security controls or leaves conflicting/failed services (final rc-status shows both services cleanly 'started'), so the impact is low, but the unexplained storage-run-1001 leftover is a genuine minor hygiene gap.
